title: Rectangular prism
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with the Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and the translation vector set to zero, zero, and zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. In this sketch, create a closed loop by drawing four lines: the first line from the origin to the point zero point one zero three four, zero; the second line from zero point one zero three four, zero to zero point one zero three four, zero point zero five one seven; the third line from zero point one zero three four, zero point zero five one seven to zero, zero point zero five one seven; and the fourth line from zero, zero point zero five one seven back to the origin. Scale this two-dimensional sketch by a factor of zero point one zero three four. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using the same Euler angles and translating it using the same translation vector. Extrude the transformed two-dimensional sketch zero point seven five units along the normal direction to create the three-dimensional model. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction. The resulting shape is a rectangular prism with rounded edges, with final dimensions of length zero point one zero three four units, width zero point zero five one seven units, and height zero point seven five units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1034, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1034, 0.0517) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0517) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the model 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.1034) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.1034) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()
